record.context_brief: Exact 1-greedy renorming of the Haar system in L^p
record.original_question: For the Haar system in L^p with 1 < p < infinity, can one find an equivalent norm under which the Haar basis becomes exactly 1-greedy, rather than merely (1 + epsilon)-greedy for each fixed epsilon > 0?

evidence.quote: Another line of study in the isometric case of greedy-type bases is the existence of renormings, that is, if my basis is C-greedy (or another type of greedy-like basis), does there exist an equivalent norm such that the basis becomes 1-greedy?

One paper where this idea is posed is [16], where the authors proved that, for a fixed epsilon > 0, it is possible to find a renorming in L^p, 1 < p < infinity, such that the Haar system is (1 + epsilon)-greedy, but it is open whether one can get the constant 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1<p<\infty$ and consider the Lebesgue space $L^p[0,1]$. The Haar system $(h_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ (normalized in $L^p$) is a Schauder basis of $L^p[0,1]$. For $f\in L^p[0,1]$ with basis expansion $f=\sum_n a_n h_n$, an $m$-term greedy approximation $G_m(f)$ is any sum $\sum_{n\in\Lambda} a_n h_n$ where $\Lambda$ is a set of $m$ indices satisfying $\min_{n\in\Lambda}|a_n|\ge \max_{n\notin\Lambda}|a_n|$. A basis is called $C$-greedy if for every $f$, every $m\ge 1$, and every greedy approximation $G_m(f)$,
$$\|f-G_m(f)\| \le C\,\sigma_m(f),$$
where $\sigma_m(f)=\inf\{\|f-g\|: g=\sum_{n\in A}b_n h_n,\ |A|\le m\}$ is the best $m$-term approximation error. A basis is $1$-greedy when this holds with $C=1$.

It is known that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a norm on $L^p[0,1]$ equivalent to the usual $L^p$ norm under which the Haar system is $(1+\varepsilon)$-greedy.

Question: Does there exist an equivalent norm on $L^p[0,1]$ under which the Haar system is exactly $1$-greedy?
artifact.category_tag: Greedy bases and renormings in Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: A 2026 preprint establishes that for each $1<p<\infty$, the $L_p$-normalized Haar system admits an equivalent renorming of $L^p[0,1]$ under which it becomes isometrically (i.e., $1$-)greedy, resolving the problem in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: Isometric renormings for greedy bases in Banach spaces, with applications to the Haar System in L_p[0,1], 1<p<∞
status_evidence.snippet: The $L_p$-normalized Haar system can be made 1-greedy under an equivalent norm for each 1<p<∞, resolving a long-standing problem.
status_evidence.claim: An equivalent norm on L^p[0,1] making the Haar system exactly 1-greedy is constructed.
